headline: Rhode Island approves winter electric-bill credits for more than 450,000 customers
dek: The three-month credits will total $61.35 per eligible residential account, with additional savings expected from a separate rate settlement.
body: Rhode Island residential electric customers will receive a series of winter bill credits after the state's Public Utilities Commission approved a $28 million relief plan, Gov. Dan McKee's office announced Thursday.

The plan calls for Rhode Island Energy customers with eligible residential A-16 and A-60 accounts to receive a $20.45 credit in January, February and March 2027. The three credits total $61.35 per account and are expected to reach more than 450,000 customers statewide.

The credits will be paired with about $14 per month beginning in October under a separate hold-harmless settlement connected to PPL's acquisition of Narragansett Electric. During the three winter months, the two programs are expected to provide roughly $34 in combined monthly credits, or more than $100 over the period, according to the governor's office.

McKee declared an energy-affordability emergency in July as winter supply rates were expected to rise by double digits. The emergency plan directs $28 million in available Regional Greenhouse Gas Initiative auction reserves to uniform residential credits while existing RGGI-funded programs continue. The administration says the two relief efforts, along with other measures, will provide nearly $200 million in direct energy-bill relief to Rhode Island customers.
